title: can this be useful for game development?
author: ninjasaid13
selftext:
PartUV: Part-Based UV Unwrapping of 3D Meshes

Project Page: [https://www.zhaoningwang.com/PartUV/](https://www.zhaoningwang.com/PartUV/)

comments.author: Independent_Sea_6317
comments.body: Theoretically it can be useful, yes. I'd need to actually use it to give you a straight answer, however. Unfortunately I don't own UVPackMaster so I can't really test it out.

comments.author: xweert123
comments.body: It seems promising, but I don't have access to it in order to stress test it and see how difficult of a time it would have.

comments.author: LQ-69i
comments.body: this + a good rigging paper and hell, everyone is going to be a gamedev

comments.author: Interesting_Airgel
comments.body: Those aren't good UVs. You can use them but to have something good you wouldn't want to stick with them

comments.author: -Sibience-
comments.body: Automatic unwrapping does have some use cases, like if you needed to unwrap many 3D assets for example. However generally manual unwrapping is always going to be better as you have far more control. Automatic unwrapping is always going to be the quick and dirty option.

comments.author: superkickstart
comments.body: Sure, if it can avoid too much stretching and the seams make sense. Tools like substance painter have made the uv mapping process less demanding anyways, though, and usually, you can just auto uv anyway.

comments.author: lndoors
comments.body:
No. Most platforms like steam thankfully won't let you sell your game unless the ai content you used was not trained on copywritten material. 

So you would have to of train the ai model yourself on data that you own. I can see a minion so that's clearly not the case. 

You can still make the game, but if your intent is to sell games ai is even more useless for this task.
